semantic_controls: sequential writes are treated as a workload and storage-layer property, not a universal guarantee of lower latency
memtable durability depends on WAL and flush publication ordering
tombstones cannot be dropped until older values can no longer be resurrected
read, write and space amplification are defined with explicit numerator and denominator rather than inferred from throughput
compaction debt, cache regime and background I/O are controlled during engine comparison
group commit amortizes sync cost but does not promise lower latency for every transaction
asynchronous commit risks bounded recent data loss but differs from disabling fsync, which can risk corruption
PostgreSQL crash recovery uses REDO and MVCC transaction status; it does not run an ARIES-style physical undo phase
PostgreSQL checkpoints are paced intervals over pages dirty at checkpoint start, not a single instantaneous global flush
ACID consistency is split between engine-enforced constraints and application-defined invariants
commit acknowledgement boundary is distinguished from partial commit and external side effects
coursera: not used; deferred to module construction by owner policy
